nodes.title: Integral and normalized Satake transforms
nodes.statement: For an unramified connected reductive F-group, hyperspecial K, minimal P=TN and cocharacter lattice Lambda=T(F)/T(F)^0, define S*(f)(t)=integral_N f(tn) with vol(N intersect K)=1. It has finite support on Lambda and takes values over Z[q^-1]. With a chosen q-half in the coefficient ring, S=delta_P^(1/2) S*. The domain uses vol(K)=1 and the existing finite double-coset convolution.
hypotheses: p is invertible in the coefficient ring; q is the residue cardinality.
proofSteps: Identify T(F)/T(F)^0 with the relative cocharacter lattice using Iwasawa decomposition.
Express the N integral as finite coset sums with volumes powers of q; prove independence of subdivisions and compact support.
Use N T decomposition and Fubini on finite sums to prove multiplicativity; isolate the modulus factor rather than choosing it silently.
acceptance: For a torus N=1, the transform is the identity on the group algebra.
An arbitrary coefficient change with q invertible commutes with S*.

nodes.title: Classical Satake isomorphism
nodes.statement: Over Z[q^-1], S* identifies the spherical Hecke algebra with the twisted W0-invariant lattice algebra. nodes.title: Local pseudoroots
nodes.statement: A local pseudoroot is an element a0 of the Frobenius-coinvariant dual torus with a0 squared equal to Sigma*(q), fixed by the twisted W0 action. Choosing a square root of q constructs a pseudoroot; an even Sigma* gives a canonical one.

Evaluate the half-coroot sum after adjoining q-half and verify both conditions.

nodes.title: Canonical c-group Satake formulation
nodes.statement: In TV arXiv v1, for coefficient characteristic different from p and two, the capital C-group is (L-group times G_m) modulo the central element (Sigma*(-1),1,-1). Take the cyclotomic inverse image to define the lower c-group before forming its Frobenius fiber.

Hom_G(W,V)=V^(n), W_[L,pi] is projective and admissible over its block center, and W_[L,pi]^(n) is free of rank one over that center. This is the universal generic projective, not a universal arbitrary irreducible representation.

Compare block endomorphisms after inverting ell to Bernstein–Deligne.
Embed the center into the tensor product of type endomorphism rings and use ell-saturation to descend the equality.
Lift a derivative generator and use projectivity to prove it generates W over G.

nodes.title: Universal co-Whittaker domination
nodes.statement: For any Noetherian A and center map A_[L,pi] to A, W_[L,pi] tensor A is co-Whittaker and surjects onto every co-Whittaker A-family with that center character. A co-Whittaker family has a uniquely determined center character through its scalar endomorphisms. Domination does not assert that every quotient is isomorphic to the universal object.
proofSteps: Base-change the free derivative and use the universal essentially AIG dual fibers.
Choose a derivative generator in V and lift it through Whittaker representability.
A nonzero cokernel would have a nonzero fiber quotient without generic constituent, contradicting the essentially AIG dual condition.
acceptance: The center character determines the universal dominating object, not a unique arbitrary co-Whittaker quotient.

nodes.title: Reconstruction from minimal-prime fibers
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced Noetherian algebra over the block center and choose nonzero generic-cosocle quotients V_a of the universal fibers at its finitely many minimal primes. The image of the diagonal universal map in the product of V_a is co-Whittaker, A-torsion-free and uniquely determined by these generic fibers in the sense of Helm Lemma 6.4.
proofSteps: Use reducedness to embed A into the product of its minimal-prime fraction fields.
Take the diagonal image and show its derivative is exactly the diagonal copy of A.
Use the fiber quotient property and Nakayama to establish co-Whittaker generation and the uniqueness image property.
acceptance: Reducedness is essential; no nilpotent information is recovered by minimal-prime fibers.

nodes.title: The conditional local-Langlands family construction
nodes.statement: Let A be a reduced complete Noetherian local ell-torsion-free W(k)-algebra with residue field k, and rho:G_F to GL_n(A) a continuous Galois representation. Assuming Helm v1 Conjecture 7.4 for rho modulo the maximal ideal, Theorem 7.8 constructs the unique admissible A-torsion-free co-Whittaker pi(rho). At every minimal prime a its fiber is the kappa(a)-dual of the Breuil–Schneider representation of the dual rho_a. This source does not prove the general interpolation conjecture.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed of characteristic ell different from p, as in Helm; rho is continuous for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on A.
proofSteps: Specify the center character only under the interpolation hypothesis.
Apply the reduced-family diagonal-image construction to the dual Breuil–Schneider generic fibers.
Apply EH uniqueness to a torsion-free co-Whittaker family with these fibers.

nodes.title: Endomorphisms after arbitrary coefficient tensoring

nodes.title: Integral invariants and duality safeguards

nodes.title: Ext and exact supercuspidal support
nodes.statement: For irreducible admissible representations of GL_n or its Levi over a field of characteristic different from p, nonzero Ext^i implies the same exact supercuspidal support. In a supercuspidal block the Laurent-coordinate maximal ideals kill Ext, so distinct unramified twists have zero Ext; inertial equivalence alone is insufficient for nonvanishing.
proofSteps: For supercuspidal types identify the block with a Laurent polynomial algebra and use two distinct maximal ideals annihilating Ext.
Induct on Ext degree through embeddings into cuspidal induction, using exact Jacquet functors and the appropriate field adjunction.
Use admissible duality for the second variable and propagate to arbitrary irreducibles.
acceptance: This field proof uses the field theory supplied earlier; it does not make SR.5 depend circularly on general SR.6 second adjointness.

nodes.title: The distinct-eigenvalue local block
nodes.statement: In the Calegari–Geraghty setup, A=O/varpi^k, q congruent to 1 modulo ell and residual unramified Frobenius eigenvalues distinct. There is a unique irreducible unramified principal series pi attached to the residual semisimple parameter. The locally admissible category with every irreducible subquotient pi is equivalent to the direct-limit finite-length module category of the completed ordered-character deformation algebra: independent pro-ell residual-unit cyclic variables of order d and independent formal unramified variables X_i.
proofSteps: Use distinct residual torus characters to split the geometric-lemma filtration and kill off-character Ext in every degree.
Identify each finite-length object with induction of its ordered Borel-Jacquet module by adjunction and length comparison.
Pass to the locally admissible union of finite-length objects and the completed deformation algebra.
acceptance: The formal variables act topologically nilpotently on finite-length modules; an uncompleted polynomial module category includes wrong blocks.

nodes.title: Injective cogenerators across coefficient primes
